records.question: Which island had the highest nearshore concentrations of dissolved nutrients and chlorophyll-a (Chl-*a*) in American Samoa according to in situ water samples?
ground_truth_chunks: Water samples collected around each island and atoll suggest that waters surrounding Tutuila were characterized as having the highest concentrations of dissolved nutrients and Chl-*a*in American Samoa.

The increased levels of nearshore nutrients observed around Tutuila were likely a result of this island's high elevation and associated influences on rainfall and the relatively high human population and related land-use disturbances.

records.question: How many unique macroalgal genera were recorded around Tutuila across the surveys years 2002–2010?
records.ground_truth_answer: 54 unique macroalgal genera were recorded around Tutuila.
ground_truth_chunks: Around Tutuila, the largest volcanic island in American Samoa, 54 unique macroalgal genera were recorded across the surveys years 2002–2010 (Fig. 10), whereas, at Swains and Rose, with notably smaller reef areas, only 17 and 27 genera were recorded.

records.question: What were the relative occurrences of coralline-algal disease lesions per percent crustose coralline algal cover for 2006, 2008, and 2010, and were there statistical differences among those survey years?
records.ground_truth_answer: Records indicated 0.16 lesions per percent crustose coralline algal cover ± 0.04 SE for 2006, 0.15 ± 0.04 SE for 2008, and 0.09 ± 0.03 SE for 2010; no statistical differences were detected among survey years (p = 0.41, ANOVA, F(2,185) = 0.92).
ground_truth_chunks: Records for all REA sites combined indicated a relative occurrence of 0.16 lessions per percent crustose coralline algal cover ± 0.04 SE for 2006, 0.15 ± 0.04 SE for 2008, and 0.09 ± 0.03 SE for 2010, with no statistical differences (*p* = 0.41, analysis of variance [ANOVA], F(2,185) = 0.92) detected among survey years.
Elevated site-specific occurrences were noted at Ofu & Olosega (2006) and Swains (2008), where the number of coralline-algal disease cases were an order of magnitude higher.

records.question: Which island had particularly low parrotfish biomass and what percentage of total fish biomass did parrotfishes average there?
records.ground_truth_answer: Swains — parrotfishes averaged only 2% of total fish biomass across all years.
ground_truth_chunks: Estimated parrotfish (Scaridae, herbivore) biomass was particularly low at Swains, averaging only 2% of total fish biomass across all years, compared to 11%–21% of total fish biomass observed for parrotfishes at other islands (Fig. 13).

In terms of the composition of reef-fish assemblages among islands estimated throughout all survey years, Swains had notably low biomass of primary consumers (i.e., fishes that eat algae and detritus), which accounted for only 12%–25% of total fish biomass at Swains compared to 34%–67% at all other islands (Fig. 13).

records.question: What was the mean coral cover (%) at Swains Island in 2002 according to the surveys?
ground_truth_chunks: Surveys conducted in 2002 revealed an ecosystem rich in hard corals, dominated by plating *Montipora* and branching *Pocillopora* corals. Mean coral cover was 49.6% (± 1.0 SE), far exceeding all other islandwide means recorded in American Samoa. Additionally, moderate levels of both macroalgal and crustose coralline algal cover were observed islandwide (Fig. 17).

ground_truth_chunks: This unit recorded data from March 14, 2008, to July 16, 2009. During those 17 months, the EAR at Rose recorded 20 vessel events in the vicinity of the monitoring site.
